annotationRationale: Prime exponents exclude prime n and n=4. Counting arrangements by their underlying unordered group partition proves the first factorial factor is integral. Prime/composite classification and permutation counts support the sufficiency argument.
sourceMethod: Follows the official factorization into an unordered-group counting number and n!/n², together with the distinct-factor and odd-prime-square divisibility cases. Expands the counting multiplicities and the exceptional-value checks.

review.mathCheck: The partition-count factor is integral, and n! / n² is integral for every composite n>4. Prime n=p fails because the numerator has p-exponent p−1 versus p in the denominator; n=4 fails with 2-exponents 11 versus 12. Including n=1 leaves 50−15−1=34, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official 2019 AMC 10A solution 25, pages 14–15. It retains the factorial factorization, unordered-group count and complete classification, while explicitly justifying arrangement multiplicities and the prime-square case.
review.annotationCheck: All cases are covered, including 0!=1 and the exceptional value 4. The counting interpretation and prime-power counts are reconstructible at AMC 12 level.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact prime/composite and permutation-formula links support classification and factorial arrangement counts. Prime valuations and double counting have no supplied CN links, so national coverage is background only.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 4.OA.B.4 supports factor pairs and prime/composite classification within n≤50. It does not cover factorial valuations or the partition-count integrality argument. No supplied US links cover those assessed skills or permutation counts.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: math:prime-valuations-factorials correctly captures the exclusion arguments; math:double-counting captures counting arrangements through partitions with constant multiplicity. cnm_p157 and cnm_h234 appropriately support classification and full-permutation counts.
